title: SpaTalk: Knowledge-Graph-Based Cell-Cell Communication Inference
text: SpaTalk computational framework inferring spatially resolved cell-cell communications (CCIs) spatial transcriptomics (ST) data. Published Nature Communications (2022), SpaTalk integrates graph network modeling knowledge graph approaches reconstruct ligand-receptor-target signaling networks spatially proximal cells.

title: SpaTalk: Knowledge-Graph-Based Cell-Cell Communication Inference
text: Shao, X., Li, C., Yang, H., et al. Knowledge-graph-based cell-cell communication inference spatially resolved transcriptomic data SpaTalk. Nature Communications 13, 4429 (2022). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-32111-8

title: SpaTalk: Knowledge-Graph-Based Cell-Cell Communication Inference
text: Cell-type deconvolution spot-based ST data using NNLM Spatial mapping scRNA-seq ST data Knowledge graph-based ligand-receptor-target pathway inference Permutation-based statistical validation Support single-cell spot-based ST platforms

title: SpaTalk Advanced Usage
text: vignette covers advanced usage scenarios SpaTalk, including: Custom ligand-receptor databases Alternative deconvolution methods Parallel processing optimization Working different ST platforms Troubleshooting common issues

title: SpaTalk Advanced Usage
text: can use curated LR pairs instead built-CellTalkDB:
code: # Custom LR pairs must have these columns: # - ligand: ligand gene symbol # - receptor: receptor gene symbol   # - species: "Human" or "Mouse"  custom_lrpairs <- data.frame(   ligand = c("CXCL12", "CCL2", "VEGFA"),   receptor = c("CXCR4", "CCR2", "KDR"),   species = "Human" )  # Use in find_lr_path obj <- find_lr_path(obj, lrpairs = custom_lrpairs, pathways = pathways)

title: SpaTalk Advanced Usage
code: # Custom pathways must have: # - src: source gene # - dest: destination gene (downstream) # - type: interaction type (optional)  custom_pathways <- data.frame(   src = c("CXCR4", "CXCR4", "STAT3"),   dest = c("STAT3", "AKT1", "MYC"),   type = c("activation", "activation", "transcription") )  obj <- find_lr_path(obj, lrpairs = lrpairs, pathways = custom_pathways)

title: SpaTalk Algorithm: Methodological Framework
text: spot-based ST data spot contains multiple cells, SpaTalk decomposes observed expression profile cell-type-specific contributions using Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF). Given: - X∈ℝG×SX \\mathbb{R}^{G \times S}: ST expression matrix (genes × spots) - R∈ℝG×CR \\mathbb{R}^{G \times C}: Reference expression profile (genes × cell types) deconvolution problem formulated : X≈R⋅WX \approx R \cdot W W∈ℝC×SW \\mathbb{R}^{C \times S} represents cell-type proportions per spot, subject : - Wij≥0W_{ij} \geq 0 (non-negativity) - ∑iWij=1\sum_i W_{ij} = 1 (proportions sum 1)

title: SpaTalk Algorithm: Methodological Framework
text: SpaTalk uses NNLM (Non-Negative Linear Model) package following optimization: minW≥0∥X−RW∥F2+λ∥W∥1\min_{W \geq 0} \|X - RW\|_F^2 + \lambda \|W\|_1 L1 regularization term promotes sparsity cell-type assignments.

title: SpaTalk Algorithm: Methodological Framework
text: score downstream transcription factors activated receptor, SpaTalk performs random walks gene-gene interaction (GGI) graph: Algorithm: Random Walk TF Scoring
code: Input: GGI graph G, receptor R, TF set T, n_walks, max_hop Output: TF scores  Initialize: score[tf] = 0 for all tf in T  for i = 1 to n_walks:     current = R     for hop = 1 to max_hop:         neighbors = G.neighbors(current)         if neighbors is empty: break         next = random_choice(neighbors)         if next in T:             score[next] += 1         current = next  Return: score / n_walks
